readings.title: The Frequency of Judgement
readings.subtitle: The Shepherd’s vision before the tectonic shift.
readings.text: [Amos 1:1] The words of Amos, who was among the herdsmen of Teqova, which he saw concerning Yisra’ěl in the days of Uzziyah sovereign of Yehuḏah, and in the days of Yaroḇ‛am son of Yo’ash, sovereign of Yisra’ěl, two years before the earthquake. [2] And he said, “<dq><dn>YeHoVaH</dn> roars from Tsiyon, and gives forth <dn>His</dn> voice from Yerushalayim. And the pastures of the shepherds shall mourn, and the top of Karmel shall wither.</dq>”

readings.title: The Iron Threshing Sledges
readings.subtitle: Exacting Tsedek for the crushing of Gil‛aḏ.
readings.text: [Amos 1:3] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“For three transgressions of Dammeseq, and for four, <dn>I</dn> do not turn it back, because they threshed Gil‛aḏ with threshing implements of iron. [4] “But <dn>I</dn> shall send fire upon the house of Ḥaza’ěl, and it shall consume the palaces of Ben-Haḏaḏ. [5] “And <dn>I</dn> shall break the bar of Dammeseq, and cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven, and the one who holds the sceptre from Běyth Ěḏen. And the people of Aram shall go exiled to Qir,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Wholesale Exile
readings.subtitle: Judgement for the trafficking of human cargo to Eḏom.
readings.text: [Amos 1:6] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“For three transgressions of Azzah, and for four, <dn>I</dn> do not turn it back, because they took into exile an entire exile, to surrender it to Eḏom. [7] “But <dn>I</dn> shall send fire upon the wall of Azzah, and it shall consume its palaces. [8] “And <dn>I</dn> shall cut off the inhabitant from Ashdoḏ, and the one who holds the sceptre from Ashqelon. And <dn>I</dn> shall turn <dn>My</dn> hand against Eqron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish,”</dq> said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Severed Brotherhood
readings.subtitle: Burning the palaces of the covenant-breakers.
readings.text: [Amos 1:9] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“For three transgressions of Tsor, and for four, <dn>I</dn> do not turn it back, because they surrendered an entire exile to Eḏom, and did not remember the brotherly covenant. [10] “But <dn>I</dn> shall send fire upon the wall of Tsor, and it shall consume its palaces.”</dq>

readings.title: The Unrelenting Sword
readings.subtitle: The perpetual wrath of Esaw against his brother.
readings.text: [Amos 1:11] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“For three transgressions of Eḏom, and for four, <dn>I</dn> do not turn it back, because he pursued his brother with the sword, and cast off all compassion. And his displeasure tore incessantly, and he kept his wrath forever. [12] “But <dn>I</dn> shall send fire upon Těman, and it shall consume the palaces of Botsrah.”</dq>

readings.title: The Border Expansion
readings.subtitle: The heinous violation of the womb for terrestrial gain.
readings.text: [Amos 1:13] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, <dn>I</dn> do not turn it back, because they ripped open the pregnant women in Gil‛aḏ, to enlarge their border. [14] “So <dn>I</dn> shall kindle a fire upon the wall of Rabbah, and it shall consume its palaces, with a shout in the day of battle, with a storm in the day of the whirlwind. [15] “And their sovereign shall go into exile, he and his heads together,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Desecration of the Dead
readings.subtitle: Reducing the bones of Eḏom to lime.
readings.text: [Amos 2:1] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“For three transgressions of Mo’aḇ, and for four, <dn>I</dn> do not turn it back, because he burned the bones of the sovereign of Eḏom to lime. [2] “But <dn>I</dn> shall send fire upon Mo’aḇ, and it shall consume the palaces of Qeriyoth. And Mo’aḇ shall die amid uproar, with a cry and with a voice of a shophar. [3] “And <dn>I</dn> shall cut off the judge from its midst, and kill all its heads with him,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.section: The Judgement of the Covenant Nations
readings.title: The Rejection of the Instruction
readings.subtitle: Seduced by the systemic lies of their fathers.
readings.text: [Amos 2:4] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“For three transgressions of Yehuḏah, and for four, <dn>I</dn> do not turn it back, because they have rejected <dn>את</dn> the Torah of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and did not guard <dn>His</dn> laws. And their lies after which their fathers walked lead them astray. [5] “But <dn>I</dn> shall send fire upon Yehuḏah, and it shall consume the palaces of Yerushalayim.”</dq>

readings.section: The Judgement of the Covenant Nations
readings.title: Trading Tsedek for Silver
readings.subtitle: The defilement of the Set-Apart Name at the slaughter-places.
readings.text: [Amos 2:6] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“For three transgressions of Yisra’ěl, and for four, <dn>I</dn> do not turn it back, because they sell the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of sandals, [7] who crush the head of the poor ones in the dust of the earth, and turn aside the way of the meek. And a man and his father go in to the same girl, to defile <dn>My</dn> set-apart Name. [8] “And they lie down by every slaughter-place on garments taken in pledge, and in the house of their mighty one they drink the wine of those who have been fined.

readings.section: The Judgement of the Covenant Nations
readings.title: The Eradication of the Amorites
readings.subtitle: Silencing the prophets and corrupting the dedicated Nazirites.
readings.text: [9] “Yet <dn>I</dn> destroyed <dn>את</dn> the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars. And he was as strong as the oaks, yet <dn>I</dn> destroyed his fruit from above and his roots from beneath. [10] “And <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> you up from the land of Mitsrayim, and led <dn>את</dn> you forty years through the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite. [11] “And <dn>I</dn> raised up some of your sons as prophets, and some of your young men as Nazirites. Not so? O you children of Yisra’ěl?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>[12] “But you made the Nazirites drink wine, and commanded the prophets saying, ‘Do not prophesy!’

readings.section: The Judgement of the Covenant Nations
readings.title: The Crushed Wagon
readings.subtitle: The absolute futility of human strength on the day of reckoning.
readings.text: [13] “See, <dn>I</dn> am weighed down by you, as a wagon is weighed down when filled with sheaves. [14] “And a place to flee shall perish from the swift, and the strong not fortify his power, and the mighty not save his life, [15] and he who handles the bow not stand, and the swift of foot not save, nor he who rides a horse save his life, [16] and the one potent of his heart among the mighty flee naked, in that day,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Penalty of Proximity
readings.subtitle: Known intimately by YeHoVaH, judged for every systemic crookedness.
readings.text: [Amos 3:1] Hear <dn>את</dn> this word that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken against you, O children of Yisra’ěl, against the entire clan which <dn>I</dn> brought up from the land of Mitsrayim, saying, [2] <dq>“You alone have <dn>I</dn> known of all the clans of the earth, therefore <dn>I</dn> punish you for all <dn>את</dn> your crookednesses.”</dq>

readings.section: The Physics of Cause and Effect
readings.title: The Master YeHoVaH Has Spoken
readings.subtitle: Unveiling the divine blueprint to the servants.
readings.text: [Amos 3:3] Would two walk together, without having met? [4] Does a lion roar in the forest, when he has no prey? Does a young lion give forth his voice out of his den unless he has caught? [5] Does a bird fall into a snare on the earth, where there is no trap for it? Does a snare spring up from the earth, if it has not captured prey? [6] If a shophar is blown in a city, do the people not tremble? If there is calamity in a city, shall not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> have done it? [7] For the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does no matter unless <dn>He</dn> reveals <dn>His</dn> secret to <dn>His</dn> servants the prophets. [8] A lion has roared! Who is not afraid? The Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken! Who would not prophesy?

readings.section: The Plunder of the Corrupt City
readings.subsection: The Witnesses of Ashdoḏ and Mitsrayim
readings.title: Hoarding Violence and Loot
readings.subtitle: The adversary surrounding the fractured land.
readings.text: [Amos 3:9] "Cry out at the palaces in Ashdoḏ, and at the palaces in the land of Mitsrayim, and say, ‘Gather on the mountains of Shomeron, and see the many unrests in her midst, and the oppressed ones within her. [10] But they do not know to do what is right,’ declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘these who store up plunder and loot in their palaces.’ ” [11] Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“An enemy, even all around the land! And he shall bring down your strength from you, and your palaces shall be plundered.”</dq>

readings.section: The Plunder of the Corrupt City
readings.title: Rescued from the Lion's Mouth
readings.subtitle: The shattering of the ivory houses and pagan slaughter-places.
readings.text: [12] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“As a shepherd rescues from the mouth of a lion two legs or a piece of an ear, so are the children of Yisra’ěl who dwell in Shomeron to be rescued – in the corner of a bed and on the edge of a couch! [13] “Hear and witness against the house of Ya‛aqoḇ,”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts. <dq>[14] “For in the day <dn>I</dn> visit Yisra’ěl for their transgressions, <dn>I</dn> shall also punish concerning the slaughter-places of Běyth Ěl. And the horns of the slaughter-place shall be broken, and they shall fall to the ground. [15] “And <dn>I</dn> shall strike the winter house along with the summer house. And the houses of ivory shall perish, and the great houses shall be swept away,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Cows of Bashan
readings.subtitle: Crushing the needy to fund an economy of excess.
readings.text: [Amos 4:1] Hear this word, you cows of Bashan, who are on the mountain of Shomeron, who are oppressing the poor, who are crushing the needy, who are saying to their masters, “Bring wine, let us drink!” [2] The Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sworn by <dn>His</dn> set-apartness, <dq>“See, days are coming upon you when <dn>He</dn> shall take <dn>את</dn> you away with hooks, and your descendants with fish-hooks, [3] and let you go out at the breaches, each woman before her, and you shall be cast out toward Harmon,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.subsection: The Multiplied Transgressions of Běyth Ěl
readings.title: The Sarcastic Call to Vain Worship
readings.subtitle: Loving the synthesized tradition over the Creator's commands.
readings.text: [Amos 4:4] <dq>"Come to Běyth Ěl and transgress, to Gilgal, increase transgression. And bring your slaughterings every morning, your tithes every three days. [5] “And burn an offering of thanksgiving with leaven, proclaim voluntary offerings, loudly. For you have loved this, you children of Yisra’ěl!”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Famine and Withheld Rain
readings.subtitle: The divine extraction of physical sustenance.
readings.text: [Amos 4:6] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> also gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places. But you did not turn back to <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>[7] “And <dn>I</dn> also withheld rain from you, three new moons before the harvest. Then <dn>I</dn> would send rain on one city, and on another city <dn>I</dn> would not send rain. One part was rained upon, and where it did not rain the part would dry up. [8] “Then two or three cities would wander to another city to drink water, but they were not satisfied. But you did not turn back to <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Blight, Locusts, and the Stench of the Camp
readings.subtitle: Plucked from the burning, yet persistently unrepentant.
readings.text: <dq>[9] “<dn>I</dn> have stricken <dn>את</dn> you with blight and with mildew. The creeping locust devoured your many gardens, and your vineyards, and your fig trees, and your olive trees. But you did not turn back to <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>[10] “<dn>I</dn> have sent among you a plague in the way of Mitsrayim. <dn>I</dn> have killed your young men with a sword, along with your captured horses. And <dn>I</dn> made the stench of your camps come up into your nostrils. But you did not turn back to <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>[11] “<dn>I</dn> have overthrown some of you, as <dn>Elohim</dn> overthrew <dn>את</dn> Seḏom and <dn>את</dn> Amorah, and you were like a burning stick plucked from the burning. But you did not turn back to <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Prepare to Meet Your Elohim
readings.subtitle: He who forms the mountains and commands the cosmic geometry.
readings.text: [Amos 4:12] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> am doing this to you, O Yisra’ěl. And because <dn>I</dn> do this to you, prepare to meet your <dn>Elohim</dn>, O Yisra’ěl!”</dq> [13] For look, <dn>He</dn> who forms mountains, and creates the wind, and who declares to man what <dn>His</dn> thought is, and makes the morning darkness, and who treads the high places of the earth, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts is <dn>His</dn> Name.

readings.title: The Decimated Ranks
readings.subtitle: Forsaken on her own land, structurally unfit for her purpose.
readings.text: [Amos 5:1] Hear <dn>את</dn> this word which <dn>I</dn> take up against you, this lamentation, O house of Yisra’ěl: [2] The maiden of Yisra’ěl has fallen, not to rise again. She lies forsaken on her land, with no one to lift her up. [3] For thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“The city that goes out by a thousand has a hundred left, and that which goes out by a hundred has ten left to the house of Yisra’ěl.”</dq>

readings.title: Seek YeHoVaH and Live
readings.subtitle: He who commands the celestial constellations and the seas.
readings.text: [Amos 5:4] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to the house of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“Seek <dn>Me</dn> and live, [5] but do not seek Běyth Ěl, nor enter Gilgal, nor pass over to Be’ěrsheḇa. For Gilgal shall certainly go into exile, and Běyth Ěl become a non-entity. [6] “Seek <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and live, lest <dn>He</dn> break out like fire upon the house of Yosěph, and shall consume it, with no one to quench it in Běyth Ěl. [7] “O you who are turning right-ruling to wormwood, and have cast down righteousness to the earth!”</dq> [8] <dn>He</dn> who made Kimah and Kesil, and who turns the shadow of death into morning and darkened day into night, who is calling for the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth – <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is <dn>His</dn> Name – [9] who is flashing forth destruction upon the strong, so that destruction comes upon the stronghold.

readings.title: Despising the Truth-Speaker at the Gate
readings.subtitle: Houses of hewn stone built on systemic extortion.
readings.text: [Amos 5:10] They hated the one who reproves in the gate, and they despise the one who speaks the truth. [11] Therefore, because you trample on the poor and take grain taxes from him – you have built houses of hewn stone but you are not going to dwell in them, you have planted pleasant vineyards but not drink wine from them. [12] For <dn>I</dn> know your transgressions are many and your sins are great, afflicting the righteous and accepting bribes, and turning aside the poor at the gate. [13] Therefore the wise keep silent at that time, for it is an evil time.

readings.title: Hate Evil, Love Good
readings.subtitle: Wailing in the vineyards when the Master passes through.
readings.text: [14] Seek good and not evil, so that you live. And let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts be with you, as you have spoken. [15] Hate evil and love good, and set up right-ruling in the gate. It might be that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts shows favour to the remnant of Yosěph. [16] Therefore <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, said this, <dq>“There is wailing in all open squares, and in all the streets they say, ‘Alas! Alas!’ and shall call the farmer to mourning, and skilled lamenters to wailing. [17] “And in all vineyards there is wailing, for <dn>I</dn> pass through your midst,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Longing for the Darkness
readings.subtitle: Fleeing a lion only to meet a bear.
readings.text: [Amos 5:18] Woe to you who are longing for the day of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! What does the day of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> mean to you? It is darkness, and not light, [19] as when a man flees from a lion, and a bear shall meet him; or entered his house, rested his hand on the wall, and a serpent shall bite him. [20] Is not the day of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> darkness, and not light? Is it not very dark, with no brightness in it?

readings.title: I Have Despised Your Festivals
readings.subtitle: Let right-ruling roll on like a mighty stream.
readings.text: [21] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have hated, <dn>I</dn> have despised your festivals, and <dn>I</dn> am not pleased with your assemblies. [22] “Though you offer <dn>Me</dn> ascending offerings and your grain offerings, <dn>I</dn> do not accept them, nor do <dn>I</dn> look on your fattened peace offerings. [23] “Take away from <dn>Me</dn> the noise of your songs, for <dn>I</dn> do not hear the sound of your stringed instruments. [24] “And let right-ruling roll on like water, and righteousness like a mighty stream.

readings.title: The Astral Mighty Ones
readings.subtitle: Exile beyond Dammeseq for the incorporated worship of Babylon.
readings.text: [25] “You brought <dn>Me</dn> slaughterings and meal offerings in the wilderness for forty years, O house of Yisra’ěl, [26] but you took up <dn>את</dn> Sikkuth your sovereign and <dn>את</dn> Kiyyun, your idols, your astral mighty ones, which you made for yourselves! [27] “Therefore <dn>I</dn> shall send you into exile beyond Dammeseq,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts – <dn>His</dn> Name.

readings.subsection: The Complacency of Tsiyon and Shomeron
readings.title: Lying on Beds of Ivory
readings.subtitle: Feasting while the breach of Yosěph remains unhealed.
readings.text: [Amos 6:1] Woe to those at ease in Tsiyon, and those trusting in Mount Shomeron, the distinguished ones among the chief of the nations, to whom the house of Yisra’ěl comes! [2] Pass over to Kalneh and see, and from there go to Ḥamath the great. Then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are you better than these reigns, or is their border greater than your border? [3] You who are putting off the day of evil, yet bring near the seat of violence, [4] who are lying on beds of ivory, and are stretched out on your couches, and are eating lambs from the flock and calves from the midst of the stall, [5] who are singing to the sound of the harp, having composed songs for themselves like Daviḏ, [6] who are drinking wine from bowls, and anoint with the finest ointments, yet they have not been pained over the breach of Yosěph! [7] Therefore they shall now go into exile, with the first of the exiles, and the feasting of the stretched-out ones shall cease!

readings.section: The Total Destruction of the Arrogant
readings.title: Striking the Great House with Breaches
readings.subtitle: A nation raised to oppress the unjust from Ḥamath to the Araḇah.
readings.text: [Amos 6:8] The Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sworn by <dn>Himself</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts declares, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am loathing <dn>את</dn> the pride of Ya‛aqoḇ, and <dn>I</dn> have hated his palaces. Therefore <dn>I</dn> shall deliver up the city and all that is in it.”</dq> [9] And it shall be, that if ten men remain in one house, they shall die. [10] And if an uncle, or his undertaker, brings the remains out of the house, he shall say to one inside the house, “Is anyone with you?” and he says, “No,” then he shall say, “Hush!” For we have not remembered the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! [11] For look, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is commanding, and <dn>He</dn> shall strike <dn>את</dn> the great house with breaches, and <dn>את</dn> the little house with clefts. [12] Do horses run on a rock? Does one plough it with oxen? For you have turned right-ruling into poison, and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood, [13] you who are rejoicing over a matter of naught, who say, “Have we not taken horns for ourselves by our own strength?” [14] <dq>“For look, <dn>I</dn> am raising up a nation against you, O house of Yisra’ěl,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts, <dq>“and they shall oppress you from the entrance of Ḥamath to the wadi Araḇah.”</dq>
